subject: Deployment mode qualification - shared vs dedicated (noisy neighbor, isolation SLOs)
messages:

- We also want to understand if Private VPC/on-prem is required for PCI workloads or whether Dedicated with certain SLAs would be sufficient.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Jordan Reed <jordan.reed@finpay.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 20:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment modes & isolation questions

Hi Alex — great talking earlier. Per our discussion, summarized below so you can share with the FinPay team. Happy to expand any section.

Summary / quick answers:
- Hosted API: fastest to launch, shared multi-tenant runtime. We provide burst protection, per-customer rate limits, and automated routing to maintain latency SLOs, but there is no dedicated GPU isolation. Good fit for development, low-risk production (non-PCI), and pilot traffic.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools for your org only. Stronger isolation (no co-tenant on the same pool), configurable autoscaling, and SLOs for throughput/latency. This is our recommended path if you need predictable p95 latency and want to avoid noisy-neighbor interference.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): customer-managed network and compute. Full isolation and compliance controls (KMS/HSM integrations, on-prem options). Recommended for regulated workloads (PCI/PHI) or when policy requires customer-managed infrastructure.

Noisy neighbor / isolation specifics (Dedicated vs Hosted):
- Dedicated: we place your workloads into reserved GPU pools (no other customers). We enforce tenant isolation at the pool level and track per-pool telemetry. If a hardware-level issue occurs we have automatic fallbacks to a cold pool and pre-warmed spill capacity.
- Hosted: we mitigate noisy neighbors with dynamic throttling, priority queuing, and request-level fairness. In extreme cases we will route critical traffic to a compatible model variant (higher-cost) to preserve SLOs.

SLOs & operational guarantees:
- Dedicated: we offer SLA-backed uptime and latency targets tied to capacity commitments; we can provide p95/p99 targets in the SOW.
- Hosted: operational SLOs are published but are best-effort for free/low-tier accounts; we can discuss contractual SLOs for paid plans.

Information we need from FinPay to recommend the right deployment:
1) Traffic profile (QPS, concurrency, payload sizes, embeddings volume) — Jordan mentioned he'll share this.
2) Latency SLO targets (p50/p95/p99) for the assistant and embedding endpoints.
3) Compliance requirements (PCI/PHI/etc) and whether customer-managed keys/on-prem are required.

Attachments: 1-pager on shared vs dedicated, SOC2 summary.

Next steps:
- Priyom / I can run a quick infra deep-dive with your platform team to size Dedicated pools and walk isolation controls.
- If PCI is required, we should discuss Private deployment options and timeline.

Proposed: 30-min technical deep-dive Wednesday or Thursday next week — I’ll send times.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

From: Jordan Reed <jordan.reed@finpay.com>

Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment modes & isolation questions

Thanks Marissa — helpful summary. Quick clarifications from our end so you can tailor the deep-dive:

- Traffic: currently ~3k requests/minute for embeddings (batched), ~350 reqs/minute for the assistant. Peak concurrency tends to be 80–120 concurrent LLM sessions. Payloads are standard (few KB).
- Latency targets: p95 <= 200ms for assistant responses (we can tolerate higher p99), embeddings p95 <= 300ms.
- Compliance: parts of our flows are PCI-scoped. Procurement will push for either Dedicated with documented isolation and KMS integration or Private VPC.
- Tolerance for noisy neighbor is effectively zero for a subset of payment flows — we need deterministic behavior.

Could you include any telemetry examples you have for Dedicated pools (p95/p99 historical), and notes on how failover works if a pool is degraded? Also curious about multi-region failover and routing.

Jordan
Jordan Reed
Platform Lead — FinPay
